title: Job cards: the workshop board
summary: Track every workshop job from intake to collection on the job cards list, with live KPIs, technician load and filters.

body.text: The **Job cards** page is the workshop's home. It lists up to 200 recent jobs and shows what each one is, whose bay it's in and who is working it. You need the *view* permission to open it; opening and editing jobs needs the *manage* permission.
Reading the KPI strip

items: **Active jobs** — everything not yet Collected or Cancelled, with a count of how many are unassigned.
**In repair** — jobs currently on the workshop floor.
**Ready for collection** — finished jobs awaiting the customer.
**Work in progress** — the billed value tied up in all active jobs.

body.text: The **Technician load** chip row below the KPIs shows how many active jobs each technician is carrying, so you can rebalance the floor at a glance.
Finding a job

items: Use the status tabs — All, Active, Awaiting approval, In repair, Ready, Collected — to narrow the list.
Type into the search box to match on job number, work description, vehicle model, VIN, registration, customer name, technician or bay.
Click a job number or **Open** to enter its workspace.

body.text: The list is scoped to what you can access. Technicians with owned-only access see just their jobs; managers with view-all see the whole floor.

title: Opening a new job card
summary: Check a vehicle in by capturing the customer request and arrival mileage; the job number and technician are set automatically.

body.text: Open a job card the moment a vehicle arrives. Use **New job card** on the job cards list, or **Book workshop** from the Service due page to pre-select the vehicle. This needs the job cards *manage* permission.

items: Select the **vehicle** — this determines the customer and where the future service history is stored.
Enter the **arrival mileage** in kilometres (optional but recommended).
Write the **work requested** so both the technician and customer understand the agreed scope — describe the concern, requested service, warning lights or noises.
Click **Open job card**.

body.text: The job number is generated automatically and the card is assigned to you as the technician. If you captured arrival mileage, it is also written to the vehicle's mileage log.
You add check-in photos, parts, labour, inspections and the customer signature inside the job workspace after it opens — not on this intake form.

title: Moving a job through its stages
summary: Every job walks a guided pipeline from Booking to Ready for collection; tap a stage to move it, or cancel and reopen as needed.

body.text: The job workspace is a guided flow. The current stage is expanded; completed and upcoming stages collapse to one-line headers you can open on demand. A stepper across the top shows the whole pipeline.
The pipeline

rows: Assign technician, bay, priority and a labour estimate
Pre-work condition photos and condition notes
Parts, labour, time clock, reservations, subcontract
Complete the job and write the service record

items: Tap any stage tile in the top stepper to move the job to that stage.
Or work down the expanded current step and let the flow guide you.
Completed stages show a green tick; the current one is highlighted.

body.text: Cancelling and reopening

items: **Cancel job** closes an in-progress job as Cancelled (an off-path terminal).
**Reopen** on a Collected or Cancelled job sends it back to Repair.
**Delete** moves the card to Trash, where it can be restored for 60 days.

body.text: Only "Complete & write service record" moves a job to Collected — tapping stages never fabricates a service record. Reaching Collected any other way is not possible from the stepper.

title: Check-in photos, condition notes and inspections
summary: Record the vehicle's pre-work condition with photos and notes, then run a multi-point inspection checklist with statuses and photos.

body.text: Check-in evidence protects both the workshop and the customer. Capture the condition **before** work starts and record what you find during diagnosis.
Check-in photos

items: In the **Check-in** step, use the camera capture or file upload to add photos of scratches, dents and the odometer.
Upload up to 12 images at a time; each must be an image under 4 MB.
Click a photo to mark it up — draw on it to highlight damage. Markup is saved as re-editable shapes plus a flattened copy for print, and the original photo is never altered.
Add **condition notes** for check-in (existing damage, charge level, loose items) and, later, check-out.

body.text: Inspection checklist

items: In the **Diagnosis** step, add a check (e.g. Brakes, Tyres, Lights, Battery terminals).
Set each item's status: OK, Attention, Fail or N/A.
Add a short note and, optionally, attach a photo to the item.
Save each row; remove a check with the ✕ button.

body.text: Check-out photos are captured later in the Quality check step to prove the hand-over condition after the work is done.

title: Logging parts, labour and technician time
summary: Add parts and labour lines, run the technician time clock, reserve stock, apply service packages and record subcontracted work.

body.text: The **Repair** step is where the job's cost is built up. Parts and labour lines drive the customer-facing total shown in the job KPIs.
Parts and labour lines

items: Add a line as either a **part** or **labour**, with a quantity and unit price.
Adding a stocked part decrements its stock; removing that line returns the stock.
Removing a line asks for a reason, which is recorded in the customer history.

body.text: The technician time clock

items: Click **Start my clock** to begin logging time against the job.
Click **Stop my clock** when you pause or finish.
Logged hours are valued at the job's labour rate (or the workshop default) to give a labour value.

body.text: A technician has only one running clock at a time. Starting a clock automatically stops any other clock you left running — on this or another job.
Reservations, packages and subcontract

items: **Reserve** earmarks stock without consuming it. **Consume** turns the reservation into a part line and deducts stock; **Release** cancels it.
**Apply service package** drops a preset bundle of parts and labour onto the job in one click.
**Subcontracted work** flags the job, records the subcontractor and cost, and feeds the profitability figure.

title: Additional-work approvals and customer sign-off
summary: Request customer approval for extra work found mid-job, record the decision, and capture the customer's signature on the card.

body.text: When you find work beyond the agreed scope, log it as an approval so the customer signs off before you proceed. This lives in the **Approval** step.

items: Enter the **additional work** description and an estimated cost, then click **Request approval**.
The customer is notified in their portal that work needs their approval.
When they respond, click **Approve** or **Decline** — the decision is recorded with the method (e.g. phone) and time.
Remove an approval line with the ✕ button if it was raised in error.

body.text: Customer signature
The signing block on the same step captures the customer's sign-off on the job card itself. Once signed, the signature and signer name are stored against the card.
Approvals track a status of pending, approved or declined. Anything still pending is surfaced on the job list under the "Awaiting approval" filter.

title: Completing a job and writing the service record
summary: Finish a job to create the vehicle's service record, set next-due values, record warranty recovery and flag comebacks.

body.text: Completing a job in the **Ready for collection** step writes a permanent service record on the vehicle and moves the card to Collected.

items: Confirm the **mileage** at completion.
Set **next due (km)** and **next due (date)** — leave them blank to auto-fill from the vehicle's service intervals.
Write a **service summary** and any **work done / notes**.
Click **Complete & write service record**.

body.text: Completion also logs the mileage, sends the customer a service review request and triggers the post-service survey. From here you can print the job and open a **Service report**.
Warranty recovery and comebacks

items: **Warranty recovery** — tick if the work is under warranty and record the labour and parts amount recovered.
**Comeback / repeat repair** — link this job to the earlier job on the same vehicle that it is a repeat of, so comeback rates stay accurate.

body.text: If you leave next-due km or date blank, the system adds the vehicle's service interval (kilometres and months) to set the next service automatically.

title: Workshop insights
summary: See work-in-progress value, 90-day profitability and comeback rate, warranty recovered and technician productivity in one place.

body.text: **Workshop insights** (linked from the job cards list) rolls up the numbers a workshop manager watches. Figures are scoped to the jobs you can access.

items: **Work in progress** — billed value tied up in active jobs, with the active job count.
**Profit · 90 days** — gross profit and margin on jobs completed in the last 90 days.
**Comeback rate · 90 days** — share of completed jobs linked as repeat repairs.
**Warranty recovered · 90 days** — total recovered on warranty work.

body.text: Below the tiles, **Technician productivity** lists hours logged per technician over the last 30 days, and **Active jobs by stage** shows how the current workload is distributed across the pipeline.
Profit is revenue less parts cost and any subcontract cost, so keep part costs and subcontract figures on job cards accurate for these numbers to hold.

title: The workshop calendar
summary: View and manage workshop bookings on a calendar that shows only workshop-category work and tracks slot capacity per day.

body.text: The **Workshop calendar** shows workshop bookings on a month view, separate from the sales diary. Only planned and completed workshop-category work appears; cancelled work is hidden.

items: Each booking shows its type and who it is assigned to.
Day capacity is tracked against configured booking slots, so you can see how full each day is.
Capacity maths counts every booking in the window, including ones assigned to other technicians, so open slots are accurate.

body.text: You need calendar or job-card view access to open it. Creating and editing bookings requires the activities manage permission.

title: Service due: staying ahead of scheduled work
summary: See which vehicles are overdue or due soon by date or mileage, then book workshop time or send the owner a reminder.

body.text: The **Service due** page lists accessible vehicles that need a service, driven by each vehicle's service intervals, last service record and latest recorded mileage.
How due status is worked out

items: **Overdue** — the next-due date has passed or the vehicle is past its next-due kilometres.
**Due soon** — within 30 days, or within 200 km, of the next service.
Explicit next-due values on the last service record win; otherwise the vehicle's interval (months and km) is applied from the last service or purchase date.

body.text: Each row shows the due date, kilometres remaining, last service and how many days early or overdue it is. The top cards count Overdue, Due soon and Total to action.
Acting on a due vehicle

items: Click **Book** / **Book workshop** to open a new job card with the vehicle pre-selected.
Or use the reminder button to send the owner a service reminder.

body.text: The book and reminder actions appear only if you have the vehicles manage permission. Everyone with view access can see the due list.

title: Warranty and recalls
summary: Monitor expiring warranties and open claims, and publish recall or service bulletins that notify affected owners.

body.text: The **Warranty & recalls** page brings together warranty status, open claims and safety bulletins for the vehicles you can access.
Warranties and claims

items: **Warranties expiring or expired** — a warranty is flagged as expiring within 60 days of its end date (purchase date plus warranty months).
**Open warranty claims** — active claims with a status of open or approved. Open the claim's print view to produce a claim document.
Claims themselves are opened and updated from the individual vehicle's page.

body.text: Recalls and service bulletins

items: Enter a **title**, choose the **affected model** and describe what owners need to know, then **Create bulletin**.
Use the notify action to email or SMS every owner of that model, at no charge to them; the bulletin records when owners were notified.
Delete a bulletin once it is no longer needed.

body.text: Creating bulletins, notifying owners and managing claims require the warranty manage permission. With view-only access you can see the dashboard but not act on it.

title: Workshop settings: rate, bays and packages
summary: Set the default labour rate, define the physical bays jobs are scheduled into, and build reusable service packages.

body.text: **Settings → Workshop** configures the defaults the rest of the workshop relies on. It requires the workshop manage permission.
Default labour rate
This rate (per hour) values the technician time logged on job cards. Individual job cards can override it in their labour estimate. The built-in default is R650/hour until you change it.
Workshop bays

items: Click **New bay** and give it a name, colour, sort order and optional notes (e.g. lift, alignment, diagnostics).
Keep **Active** ticked to make the bay available for assignment.
Edit or delete bays as your floor changes — deleting a bay unassigns any job cards in it.

body.text: Service packages

items: Click **New package** (e.g. "Minor service") and describe what it includes.
Add line items as parts or labour with a quantity and unit price; the package total updates automatically.
Technicians can then apply the whole bundle to a job card in one click from the Repair step.

body.text: Bays and their colours flow straight through to the job list and job workspace, so a quick glance shows what each work area is doing.
